items.title: Selangor Wholesale Market operations continue despite fire
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Wholesale Market in Seri Kembangan is operating as usual, with business activities unaffected by a fire on July 23. The Selangor Agricultural Development Corporation (PKPS) said the fire did not involve the main building housing daily operations and traders' activities, while the cause of the incident remains under investigation. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar confirmed the fire did not affect the main building and firefighting operations were completed at 6am yesterday.

items.title: PM: Malaysia's halal certification should be backed by industry capabilities
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Malaysia has the potential to emerge as a global halal industry hub if its internationally recognised halal certification system is backed by robust industry capabilities and strategic international collaboration. He said several world leaders he had met had expressed interest in collaborating with Malaysia in the halal sector, including obtaining the country's halal certification. However, Anwar said Malaysia could not rely solely on the strength of its halal certification, but must instead build a more comprehensive halal industry ecosystem.

items.title: Lawyer files police report over alleged bullying at school linked to Zara Qairina case
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A lawyer representing a child in a bullying case involving the late Zara Qairina Mahathir has lodged a police report regarding another alleged bullying incident at the same school. Datuk Ram Singh, who represents Student A in the Kota Kinabalu Children's Court and at the Coroner's Court inquest into Zara Qairina's death, lodged the report at the Luyang police station today. He urged police to investigate whether relevant authorities implemented anti-bullying measures at the Papar school following the incident involving Zara Qairina, who was found unconscious on July 16 last year.

items.title: Najib Razak undergoes coronary procedure; no stent needed, doctors confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Former Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is in stable condition and recovering after undergoing a coronary angiogram today, with doctors confirming that no further surgical intervention, such as balloon angioplasty or stent implantation, is required. According to a statement released by his legal counsel, Messrs Shafee & Co., the medical procedure was deemed necessary following a series of health evaluations over the past several weeks. The medical team had previously advised that there was an estimated 95% probability that Najib would require further intervention.

items.title: GPS device, fish finder for registered Melaka fishermen expected by end of August
items.summary: MELAKA: Global Positioning System (GPS) technology devices and fish finders for use by registered fishermen in Melaka are expected to be obtained by the end of August at the latest. State Rural Development, Agriculture and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said that the use of the technology, which is expected to benefit around 1,000 fishermen, involves an allocation of RM1 million provided by the state government. Dr Akmal also said that 60,000 Melaka Jagung Manis cobs will also be distributed for free to Melaka AgroFest 2026 visitors throughout the three days.

items.title: Malaysia must intensify fight against drug abuse before we lose another generation
items.summary: LETTER: The persistent and growing problem of drug abuse in Malaysia is a matter of utmost seriousness and warrants national concern. Despite decades of enforcement, rehabilitation programmes and public awareness campaigns, drug abuse continues to spread, particularly among young people. Declare drug abuse, especially synthetic drug abuse, a national priority with stronger coordination among all relevant ministries and agencies.

items.title: Sanusi warns of lawsuits, police reports over ‘distorted’ speech
items.summary: ALOR SETAR — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has warned that he will take legal action, including filing civil suits, against anyone found to be twisting his remarks for political gain, according to a report by Sinar Harian. Acccording to Sinar Harian , Sanusi told reporters he would lodge police reports against those he accused of distorting comments he made during a ceramah in Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, insisting his remarks were purely factual. Zahid said such remarks could stir unease among communities and suggested Sanusi focus instead on managing Kedah’s affairs ahead of polling day.

items.title: KM Bendahara bolsters Malaysia's maritime capabilities in Sabah, South China Sea
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The deployment of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency's (MMEA) latest offshore patrol vessel KM Bendahara is expected to strengthen the country's enforcement, surveillance and operational readiness, particularly in the waters off Sabah and the South China Sea. The vessel was officially named at the MMEA Bendahara Naming Ceremony, launched by Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman here today. In his speech, Awang Alik said the commissioning of KM Bendahara demonstrates the Madani government's continued commitment to strengthening national maritime security by enhancing strategic assets to address increasingly complex security challenges.

items.title: BN has no objection to TH RCI report release, says Tok Mat
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional has no objection to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji being tabled in Parliament or released to the public if the Cabinet decides to do so. Its deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the RCI report was an important investigative document prepared by a commission appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, adding that any follow-up action arising from its findings was a matter for the government. The report can be tabled in Parliament or released to the public, but it must follow proper procedures and receive Cabinet approval," he said after appearing on Podcast Utama Buletin TV3 in conjunction with the Negri Sembilan election.

items.title: Police launch 16 probes into alleged election-related offences in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan police have received 16 reports and opened 11 investigation papers, including two opened yesterday, over alleged election-related offences in the state polls. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in the loss or damage of property. However, Alzafny said the security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.

items.title: Kemas staff may get permanent positions under new service scheme, says Zahid
items.summary: "I have instructed Kemas director-general Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man to look into a new service scheme for all Kemas teachers, with better salaries and more attractive offers. "The existing service scheme approved by the Public Service Department places Kemas teachers on contract. He said this when launching the Negri Sembilan-level Hari Kemas and Alpha Gen Talent @Kemas programme here today.

items.title: Family, including baby, rescued from Tanjung Kling flash floods
items.summary: Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said seven firefighters from the Tangga Batu Fire and Rescue Station were deployed after the department received an emergency call at 9.47am. Meanwhile, Melaka Civil Defence Force (APM) director Lt Col (PA) Kamarulsyah Muslim said continuous heavy rain since 1 am caused several flood-prone areas in Melaka Tengah to be inundated. Kamarulsyah, who is also the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat spokesperson, said no temporary relief centre had been opened and no victims evacuated as of 10 am.

items.title: Teen's automotive dreams cut short in fatal Karak crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The aspirations of 17-year-old S. K. Kiisven to pursue a career in the automotive industry were cut short after he died in an accident at Km 86 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur–Kuantan near Karak early today. The victim's father, C. Sasi Kumar, 47, said his second child was pursuing a skills course at a vocational academy in Karak, Bentong. However, he always returned home every weekend," he said when met at the Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital Forensic Medicine Unit here today.

items.title: Sanusi claims Tanah Melayu remarks twisted for political gain, ready to take legal action
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor insisted that his remarks on Tanah Melayu being the sole homeland for Malays, made during a ceramah in Negri Sembilan, had been twisted for political gain. The Kedah Menteri Besar, who is also Perikatan Nasional election director, said he would take legal action, including filing lawsuits, against any individual or party that deliberately manipulated his remarks. Do not attempt to distort the facts," he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan cooperation with Perikatan does not bind BN, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Barisan Nasional’s cooperation with Perikatan Nasional in the Negeri Sembilan state election is only a political understanding and does not amount to a formal agreement, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said. According to Utusan Malaysia , Ahmad said there was no formal pact at the state level, leaving Umno and BN free to determine the strategies they considered best to remain relevant and win the election. “At the state level, there is no agreement.

items.title: Suspect arrested in Shah Alam for armed van heist attempt
items.summary: South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the remand application for the local suspect in his 20s, was made at the Klang Court yesterday. “The court then granted the suspect a six-day remand starting yesterday until July 29,” he said via a Whatsapp message today. Earlier, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M Kumar said the local suspect, in his 20s, was arrested in Shah Alam, Selangor at 11 am, July 23.

items.title: Melaka floods: Emergency shelters set up after relentless rain
items.summary: MELAKA, July 25 —Two temporary relief centres have been opened after heavy rain caused flooding in several areas in the Melaka Tengah and Jasin districts as of 3 pm today. Continuous heavy rain since early this morning has caused flooding in several areas in Melaka Tengah, namely Kampung Lereh, Peringgit, Kampung Bachang, Kampung Kolam Limbongan, Tengkera, Bukit Rambai, Tanjung Kling, Pengkalan Perigi and Kampung Berlian. In Jasin, the affected villages are Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: Immigration detainees first to undergo Refugee Registration Document screening
items.summary: PARIT BUNTAR: Immigration detainees nationwide will be the first group to undergo screening under the government's newly introduced Refugee Registration Document initiative. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move would allow authorities to conduct comprehensive verification and security screening before deciding whether individuals claiming refugee status were eligible for recognition. He said there were currently about 21,000 occupants at immigration depots nationwide, with around 4,000 claiming to be refugees.

items.title: Calls for Malays to unite must go on, Sanusi’s speech taken out of context, says Annuar Musa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Calls by leaders for Malays to unite, remain united and love their homeland must continue, Tan Sri Annuar Musa said today as he defended Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks that have drawn criticism for their racial tone. In a Facebook post, Annuar said Sanusi’s remarks had been taken out of context and denied that the PAS leader had intended to hurt the feelings of other ethnic communities in Malaysia. That is completely untrue.” he said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: BN 'copy-pasted' PH manifesto, says Aminuddin
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has claimed that the Barisan Nasional manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election largely copied initiatives previously introduced and implemented by the Pakatan Harapan (PH) state government under his leadership. The caretaker menteri besar said his administration had fulfilled the promises made in PH's manifesto, proving that commitments once dismissed by critics had since become a reference point for BN's own manifesto. "When we launched our manifesto before, they said my promises could never be fulfilled.

items.title: Halal certification opens wider market opportunities for entrepreneurs - Perlis Raja Muda
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: Halal certification can enhance consumer confidence, strengthen brand reputation and open wider market opportunities for entrepreneurs, said Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail. He said the certification reflected entrepreneurs' commitment to ensuring their products and services complied with Islamic requirements while meeting established quality, safety and hygiene standards Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra urged entrepreneurs in the state to seize the opportunity to obtain halal certification as a strategic move to strengthen business competitiveness. He said the authorities should continue playing a proactive role in facilitating entrepreneurs' efforts to encourage greater participation in halal certification applications, thereby strengthening the halal ecosystem in Perlis.

items.title: Schoolgirls' families searched abandoned flats before bodies discovered
items.summary: Security guard R. Madhesh, 22, said the brother of one of the victims arrived around 2.30pm with a friend on a motorcycle to look for his sister. "About an hour later, the guardian of one of the girls arrived by car," he said. I said no, although his friend had said he saw them enter at 1.30pm.

items.title: Malaysia’s GNI per capita hits record high, ‘one step away’ from high-income nation, says HR minister
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, July 25 — Malaysia is now just one step away from achieving high-income nation status based on the World Bank's per capita income threshold, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Malaysia's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, measured using the World Bank Atlas method, has reached US$12,380 (about RM50,640), the highest level since independence. He said the country's economic size, measured by Gross Domestic Product (GDP), has also increased to US$472 billion, also the highest value since 1957.

items.title: Prisons Dept taps inmates' TVET skills for community projects
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the department's approach under the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes was unique, as it involved inmates, or prospects, in carrying out infrastructure projects for local communities. Unlike other agencies that typically engage contractors, he said the Prisons Department mobilised prospects who had undergone skills training to contribute to such projects. Saifuddin said this after launching the Prisons Department's Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes at Dewan PDT Tanjung Piandang here today.

items.title: Anwar: Bullying has no place in schools
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today voiced concern over bullying in schools, urging educators to treat every case seriously. Anwar said he was deeply troubled whenever he was informed of bullying incidents, stressing that such behaviour was incompatible with the values the education system sought to instil. It should never happen," he said.

items.title: ‘Malaysia is their home’: Azalina says Constitution protects rights of non-Malays alongside Malays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said today said racial rhetoric had no place in the Negeri Sembilan election campaign, as she criticised remarks by Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. Azalina said such rhetoric could create the impression that Malaysians of Chinese and Indian descent had other homelands, while only Malays truly belonged in Malaysia. Malaysia is their homeland,” she said.

items.title: Aminuddin challenges BN manifesto, says Negeri Sembilan has already met RM30b investment target
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan’s economic performance under the Pakatan Harapan (PH) administration, particularly in terms of investment, has surpassed the target set by Barisan Nasional (BN) in its manifesto for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, said state PH chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun. He said BN’s target of RM30 billion in investments over five years did not reflect the state’s current economic performance, as Negeri Sembilan had achieved the target. The Negeri Sembilan BN manifesto, launched yesterday, targets RM30 billion in investments over five years if the coalition is given the mandate to govern the state.

items.title: School liaison officers first point of contact for students, parents
items.summary: PARIT BUNTAR: School liaison officers remain key to enhancing school safety. They go beyond addressing bullying cases and serve as the first point of contact for students, parents and school authorities, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. "We place school liaison officers in schools.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin presents Perak King's Scout Awards
items.summary: IPOH: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah today graced the presentation of the King's Scout Award, decorations, medals and certificates for the state's Scouts Association of Malaysia (PPM) branch. Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Chief Scout Maj-Gen Prof Datuk Mohd Zin Bidin. The BSR-E is the third-highest award of the Scouts Association of Malaysia, presented to individuals who have rendered distinguished service to the scout movement.

items.title: Former COO loses unfair dismissal claim over 'stealth' company venture
items.summary: Industrial Court chairman Chow Siew Lin ruled that Advent Packaging Sdn Bhd had just cause to dismiss Ooi Tse Biing after finding that he had set up and operated SG Film Sdn Bhd (SG Film) without the company's consent and authorisation, breaching his employment contract. Ooi, who earned RM50,000 a month as the company's chief operating officer (COO), claimed he had been unfairly dismissed. According to the court document, Ooi's dismissal arose from his alleged misconduct as the COO by setting up another company, SG Film Sdn Bhd (SG Film), "without the consent and authorisation of the company while he was still employed."

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi demands RM5mil over alleged defamation linking him to TH
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki is seeking RM5 million in damages from two individuals whom he accused of defaming him by linking him to an issue involving Tabung Haji. In a Facebook post, Asyraf said he had instructed his lawyer, Datuk Adnan Seman, to issue letters of demand (LOD) to Amanah central leadership council member Datuk Dr Ismail Salleh and social media account owner Abied Abdullah over the alleged defamatory claims. He said the LODs demanded that both individuals publicly apologise, retract the alleged defamatory statements, provide an undertaking and pay RM5 million in damages.

items.title: Police open 11 investigation papers over election offences in Negri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan police have opened 11 investigation papers and received 16 reports regarding alleged election-related offences in the state polls, including two opened yesterday. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in property loss or damage. However, Alzafny said the overall security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.

items.title: BN manifesto offers practical roadmap for Negri's revival, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional's manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election offers a practical and realistic blueprint to revive programmes that were left unfinished after BN lost power, says chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the manifesto, launched by state BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan last night, was built on foundations laid during BN's previous administration and could be implemented immediately should the coalition return to power. "Whoever leads Negri Sembilan after the election should take into account what has been outlined in the BN manifesto.

items.title: 144,894 smallholders approved for Budi Agrikomoditi assistance, says minister
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said a total of 144,894 smallholders had been approved to receive the Budi Agrikomoditi assistance scheme as of July 15. Noraini said the figure was the highest number of approvals recorded by any ministry under the government's targeted diesel subsidy initiative. Noraini said the ministry also provided information on the Budi Agrikomoditi scheme throughout the programme.

items.title: PM Anwar condemns Kedah MB Sanusi’s divisive comments, calls for unity
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has strongly condemned Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks suggesting that different ethnic groups in Malaysia could fall back on ancestral homelands outside the country. According to FMT, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said no leader should make statements that could offend other races, stressing that the Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities are loyal citizens who respect the Federal Constitution. "The Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities respect the constitution and are loyal citizens.

items.title: Malaysia women-only trains gain global attention after French documentary feature
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's public rail network has captured international attention after being featured in the French travel documentary series Des trains pas comme les autres (Amazing Train Journeys). "In the Kuala Lumpur metro in Malaysia, certain carriages are reserved exclusively for women. Another user, @damien_mikeng, said the initiative reflected Malaysia's cultural values.

items.title: ‘There is no need to come to Negeri Sembilan’: Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 25 — Deputy Prime Minister and Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor to steer clear of racial and religious sentiments during the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign. Astro Awani reported Zahid, Speaking to reporters after launching the “Madani Agriculture Commodity Programme” in Kuala Pilah today, said that if Sanusi truly wished to promote national unity, he should avoid touching on issues related to ethnicity, religion, culture or other racial backgrounds, as such remarks could stir unease among various communities. Zahid noted that Sanusi, who is also PAS’s election director for the state polls, may be accustomed to addressing Kedah’s electorate, but his style of speech may not sit well with the more diverse voters of Negeri Sembilan, where his words could be misinterpreted and cause unnecessary tension.

items.title: 'No need to come to Negri': Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah, avoid divisive rhetoric
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor not to stir up racial and religious sensitivities in Negri Sembilan ahead of its state election. Zahid said the Kedah menteri besar should stay in Kedah for the remainder of the campaign period and focus on governing his state instead of campaigning in Negri Sembilan. Let us manage Negri Sembilan in our own way."

items.title: Rights body Suhakam voices concern over court ruling denying citizenship to children born out of wedlock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has expressed deep concern over a recent Court of Appeal decision that denies Malaysian citizenship to children born out of wedlock to Malaysian fathers and non-Malaysian mothers. While affirming full respect for judicial independence and acknowledging the court’s role in interpreting the Federal Constitution as it stands, Suhakam said the ruling exposes critical gaps in the country’s citizenship framework that could leave vulnerable children at risk of statelessness. “Every child has the right to acquire a nationality,” Suhakam said in a statement today, citing Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), to which Malaysia has been a signatory since 1995.

items.title: Anwar rejects Sanusi's 'Tanah Melayu' remarks, says Malaysia must embrace all citizens
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's remarks on Tanah Melayu, saying Malaysia's strength lies in embracing all citizens. Anwar said Malaysia, independent for nearly 70 years, should not have leaders making statements that could insult or exclude other communities. He said while Malays were historically associated with Tanah Melayu, Malaysia's citizens came from diverse ancestral backgrounds and all who accepted the Constitution and contributed to the country must be regarded as part of the nation.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia given two years to tighten laws on forced labour imports under US trade deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Malaysia will have two years to introduce measures prohibiting imports of goods produced using forced labour under its trade agreement with the US, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said today. He said the Human Resources Ministry had been informed of the changes required, including measures aimed at preventing Malaysian exports from incorporating imported materials or components produced through forced labour in third countries. Johari also addressed the US’ decision to impose a 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian imports following its investigation into countries that did not impose and effectively enforce restrictions on imports of goods produced using forced labour.

items.title: Loke urges NS election rivals to campaign positively, avoid arrogance
items.summary: JELEBU: All parties contesting the Negri Sembilan election should campaign positively and avoid arrogant statements DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the ultimate decision on the fate of any candidate or party rested entirely with the voters. We should campaign positively. "The local people know better than Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid.

items.title: China evacuates 20,000 people as Typhoon Noul nears
items.summary: BEIJING: Authorities have evacuated more than 20,000 people and suspended railway services in southern China as Typhoon Noul approaches, threatening torrential rain and gale-force winds, according to state media. The typhoon is forecast to make landfall along the coastal area stretching from Hong Kong to Guangdong province between Saturday evening and Sunday morning, China's National Meteorological Center said. Guangdong will suspend some train services on Saturday morning, with all rail services in the province to be halted on Sunday, CCTV said.

items.title: Anwar says decision on potential Formula One return to Malaysia will be announced tomorrow
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said developments regarding the possibility of Malaysia returning as a host for a Formula One (F1) race this year will be announced tomorrow. “The F1 matter will be announced on Sunday,” he said briefly when met by reporters after officially opening Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin and launching the Nuqaba programme here today. Yesterday, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the ministry was actively discussing and assessing the possibility of Malaysia hosting the race to replace the Bahrain Grand Prix, which is scheduled to take place in October.

items.title: Govt absorbs higher oil costs to keep RON95 at RM1.99, says Anwar
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is maintaining the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 despite rising global oil prices by spending up to RM50 billion a year on fuel subsidies, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the government continued to shield consumers from higher fuel costs by absorbing billions of ringgit in subsidies, even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pushed up crude oil prices and import costs. Anwar said Putrajaya was expected to spend between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually on fuel subsidies to keep pump prices low.

items.title: Man arrested over seditious, insulting Facebook post against Islam
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested a man for allegedly uploading a Facebook post containing seditious and insulting remarks against Islam. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged at 12.38am yesterday after a member of the public spotted the viral post on social media. "Checks showed that the owner of a Facebook account under the name 'Fadzil Zahari' shared several screenshots believed to have been uploaded by account owner 'Parthiban Ragu', which contained statements insulting Islam as well as offensive and obscene expressions directed at Allah SWT and Prophet Muhammad SAW.

items.title: Take a hard look at yourselves before lecturing Malaysians on unity, Kasthuri tells Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Perikatan Nasional and PAS should “walk the talk” on national unity before lecturing Malaysians about it, DAP’s Kasthuri Patto said today, as she criticised the use of racial rhetoric during the Negeri Sembilan election campaign. “Malaysians must reject politicians who manipulate and exploit race and religion for their own political survival,” she said in a statement. Kasthuri was responding to remarks by PN election director and Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor, as well as Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, which she said had brought racial considerations into the campaign.

items.title: No one above the law, says Anwar, expects Cabinet nod to release Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said no individual was above the law, as he stressed his government’s commitment to combating corruption and strengthening governance. Anwar also said he expects the Cabinet to agree to make the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Tabung Haji public when he tables the matter on Wednesday. “Maybank had also received global recognition for corporate governance and responsibility,” he said.

items.title: Take a leaf out of MIC’s book, DAP MP tells MCA over response to Sanusi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — DAP’s Chong Zhemin has questioned MCA’s silence over racial remarks made by Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. According to Free Malaysia Today , the Kampar MP said MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran had already spoken out against the remarks despite Barisan Nasional’s electoral cooperation with PN in the Negeri Sembilan state election. “Yet MCA president Wee Ka Siong and the rest of the MCA leadership remain conspicuously silent.

items.title: Royal reassurance: Sultan of Terengganu in good health, continues treatment plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — The Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, is in good health and will continue his scheduled follow-up treatment abroad under the care of His Royal Highness’ medical team. The Office of the Sultan of Terengganu, in a statement shared by the Information Department today, said Sultan Mizan also expressed his deepest appreciation and gratitude to the people for their continued prayers for His Royal Highness’ health and well-being. “May Allah SWT continue to bless His Royal Highness the Sultan with good and lasting health, and ease all of his affairs,” the statement said.

items.title: Heavy fog cuts visibility in Sibu, disrupts air travel (VIDEO)
items.summary: SIBU, July 25 — Thick fog blanketed the riverine town today morning, significantly reducing visibility. Meanwhile, Deputy Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee said in a Facebook post that his flight from Kuching was unable to land in Sibu due to low cloud cover and fog at Sibu Airport. — The Borneo Post Dense fog shrouds the Rajang River in Sibu, leaving the waterway barely visible.

items.title: Police arrest student after baby’s body found at Kuala Langat hostel
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 25 — Police have arrested a female student in connection with the discovery of a baby’s body wrapped in cloth at a waste collection area of a hostel block at a higher learning institution (IPT) in Kuala Langat yesterday. Kuala Langat district police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said the teenage suspect was arrested following a report received from a local male informant regarding the discovery of the baby’s body at 12.20 pm yesterday. He urged anyone with information related to the incident to come forward at the nearest police station or contact the Kuala Langat district police headquarters (IPD) operations room at 03-3187 2222 to assist in the investigation.

items.title: Anwar urges Malaysians to consider RM50b fuel subsidy bill before listening to government critics
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — The Madani government spends between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually to keep RON95 petrol prices at RM1.99 per litre despite rising global oil prices, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said many neighbouring countries recorded significantly higher fuel prices, while the Madani government continued subsidising petrol and diesel to ease the burden on Malaysians. Besides fuel subsidies, Anwar said the government also allocates about RM15 billion to RM16 billion annually for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes.

items.title: Anwar gives ministries one month to resolve foreign worker applications, prioritising restaurants
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the relevant ministries and departments to resolve foreign worker employment application issues according to priority, particularly for the restaurant sector, within one month. “So, insya-Allah, starting from Monday, I am giving the relevant ministries and departments a maximum period of one month to resolve foreign worker issues according to priority,” he said at the launch of the Indian Muslim Transformational Framework (IMTF) 2030 at the PICCA@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre here last night. Also present were Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, Minister of Higher Education Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Minister of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Steven Sim and Pertubuhan Gabungan Mukmin Nasional (Mukmin) president Datuk Shahul Dawood.

items.title: Fahmi: ICU to coordinate RM44.5m flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya, Damansara
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 25 — The RM44.5 million allocation announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for 30 flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya and Damansara will be coordinated through the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) of the Prime Minister’s Department. Earlier at the programme, the Prime Minister said the federal and Selangor state governments had agreed to approve 30 flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya and Damansara, involving a total allocation of RM44.5 million. Anwar said the flood mitigation projects were part of the government’s efforts to address areas identified as flood hotspots in Petaling Jaya and Damansara.

items.title: Two 14-year-old girls found dead at Ipoh flats, police investigations ongoing
items.summary: IPOH, July 25 — Two 14-year-old female students were found dead at Flat Sungai Pari here yesterday afternoon. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police received a report on the incident in the afternoon and initial investigations found that the two victims had left the school before they were found unconscious and later pronounced dead at the scene. He urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Ipoh District Police Operations Room at 05-2451500 or the nearest police station to assist with the investigation.

items.title: Malaysia aims to produce first locally made human vaccine by 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Malaysia is reprotedly aiming to produce its first locally manufactured human vaccine as early as 2028, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang reportedly said. The Sta r reported Chang as saying the vaccine would be a 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, or PCV13, produced by Pharmaniaga Bhd through a technology transfer arrangement with a Chinese company. Chang reportedly said that producing vaccines locally would lessen Malaysia’s reliance on overseas supplies and improve its ability to respond to future public health crises.

items.title: Ramkarpal: Umno’s silence over PAS racial remarks may be ‘sign of things to come’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Umno’s silence over racial remarks by PAS leaders could set the tone for their new-found political cooperation in Negeri Sembilan, DAP’s Ramkarpal Singh said today. Ramkarpal said Sanusi’s remarks were insensitive to non-Malays and implied that Malaysian Indians and Chinese did not belong in the country because they could supposedly return to India or China. Ramkarpal further called on the authorities to immediately investigate Sanusi, saying failure to act risked similar remarks being repeated during the Negeri Sembilan election campaign.

items.title: Teen found dead after suspected fall from Komtar, police say no evidence of foul play
items.summary: Timur Laut police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report from a member of the public regarding the incident at 4.05pm. He said preliminary investigations identified the victim as an 18-year-old local male from the Macallum area. Abdul Rozak said preliminary investigations found no evidence of foul play.

items.title: Police bust gun-smuggling network operating for seven years, seize RM360,000 in weapons
items.summary: KANGAR, July 25 — Police have crippled a firearms smuggling syndicate after seizing weapons worth RM360,000 and arresting eight individuals, including a civil servant, in operations across Perlis, Perak, and Kedah this month. Perlis Police chief Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said the syndicate has been active since 2019. Muhammad said the crackdown began after the Perak contingent police headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID) arrested a man in Sitiawan on July 1.
